clue.text: American rotter appearing in pulpit, delivering surprise attack

indicators.note: something appearing in a place is found inside it, so one set of letters goes within the other

parts.note: an ambo is a raised pulpit or reading desk in early churches
standard abbreviation
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: An American scoundrel climbs into the pulpit and delivers a shock to the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: An ambo is the raised reading desk of early churches; the answer is an archaic form of ambuscade.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambuscado is an old word for an ambush, an attack sprung by hidden troops.

clue.text: It may involve march round centre of Goa

definitions.text: It may involve march round centre of Goa

indicators.note: turned round, the letters are spun into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the centre of a short word is its middle letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of the Indian state's name

explanation.surface: Something that might feature a parade around the middle of Goa.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a MORCHA, an Indian protest, typically involves a march, and Goa sets the scene in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A morcha is an Indian demonstration or protest procession, which usually takes the form of a march.

clue.text: Trunks that have lasted, a success? Gush about that

parts.note: boak is Scots for retch or vomit, a gush from the stomach

explanation.surface: Lasting swimming trunks would count as a triumph worth gushing about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunks' suggests swimwear; here they are tree trunks preserved in peat bogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bog oak is ancient oak timber preserved black in peat bogs for thousands of years, so its trunks have endured.

clue.text: Indication of disagreement, secret, Home Secretary regularly suppressed

explanation.surface: A secret disagreement in which the Home Secretary is kept quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: HUSH-HUSH loses its first, third, fifth and seventh letters, which are H, S, H, S, the Home Secretary twice over, leaving UH-UH.
explanation.definitionFit: Uh-uh is the informal grunt someone makes to signal no or disagreement.

clue.text: Free-swimming drifters engaged in universal pastime

explanation.definitionFit: Salpas are salps, barrel-shaped marine tunicates that drift freely in open ocean.

clue.text: Study the heavens, i.e. with moon and stars variously

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Studying the sky means looking at the moon and the stars in their various positions.
explanation.definitionFit: To astronomise is an old verb for practising astronomy, observing the celestial bodies.

clue.text: Like the newly born with being ignored bawl when pa's around

indicators.note: something placed around another surrounds it

parts.note: to bawl is to yowl
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A baby wails and its father circles anxiously, nobody paying attention.

explanation.definitionFit: A day-old infant was born only yesterday, which describes a newborn exactly.

clue.text: Common left after most of season's over

parts.note: autumn is one of the four seasons

explanation.surface: Once most of the season has passed, something ordinary is all that remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutual means shared, held in common by two or more parties.

clue.text: Family housed in short thoroughfare, stony

explanation.definitionFit: Stony, short for stony-broke, and skint are both British slang for having no money at all.

clue.text: Elegies composed in regular bits of bliss not as subject

taken as written

clue.text: Pet I ask nervously about a game, skipping do

taken as written

clue.text: The majority of seabirds in air, flying? they can decimate shoals

parts.note: gulls are common seabirds
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the gulls the predators; the real culprits are parasites.
explanation.definitionFit: Arguli are fish lice, parasitic crustaceans that infest and can kill many fish.

clue.text: Orcadian bird: it's seen returning in local common

clue.text: A cold curse involving bling gets familiar?

clue.text: Teacake with bit of glucose as sweetener

clue.text: Coaches supplying narcotic

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests drug-smuggling coaches; the two words simply define the same word separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Charas means both charabancs, early touring coaches, and cannabis resin smoked as a drug in India.

clue.text: Salt advanced to lee with altered course going about

explanation.definitionFit: An oleate is a salt or ester of oleic acid, a chemical compound.

clue.text: The good things of life (11, three words)

parts.note: surface reading: a general phrase for life's pleasures
setter's reading: the phrase names a familiar idiom built from two treats, a baked one and a drink

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a plain definition of a stock phrase, made more famous by Shakespeare's Twelfth Night and Maugham's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names pleasant food and drink, standing for enjoyment and pleasure generally.

clue.text: Source of news items to expedite, no longer postponed, one assumes? (11, two words)

parts.note: to press on something is to hurry it along

explanation.surface: A newsroom hurries out stories that are no longer delayed, one supposes.
explanation.walkthrough: PRESS + OFF ICE: 'on ice' means put on hold, and 'one assumes?' admits that OFF ICE as its opposite is an invented expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A press office issues statements and releases to journalists, supplying material for news stories.

clue.text: I had got in revenue, looking delighted

clue.text: Browning? That dallying with EB may have stirred nun's bate!

initials of Elizabeth Barrett, later Browning; these come out

explanation.surface: A poet's affair with Elizabeth Barrett might have provoked a nun's rage.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: the answer plus EB, stirred, gives NUN'S BATE. 'Browning' looks like the poet but means turning brown; bate is a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A suntan is the browning of the skin caused by exposure to sunlight.

clue.text: Between sound opposites of two cross off sound engineer's contribution?

explanation.walkthrough: A DEUX loses its X, the cross, and sits between F (forte) and P (piano).
explanation.definitionFit: A fade-up is a gradual increase in volume or picture, a technician's adjustment in broadcasting.

clue.text: Broadcast of Friends, having died out, concludes
